title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover load-shedding
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: customers observed regional failovers and aggressive load-shedding during short-lived control-plane flaps; the SLO enforcer backoff had a race that aggressively opened circuit breakers and incorrectly escalated regional failover. This hotfix tightens backoff hysteresis, fixes a race in the backoff state transition, adds a conservative load-shedding policy for degraded regions, and restores graceful degradation order to prefer reduced throughput over global failover. Changes: 1) Fix race: introduce a single-writer canonical state update in slo/enforcer/state.go and add atomic snapshot checks before transitioning to BACKOFF/OPEN. 2) Hysteresis: increase backoff smoothing window from 30s to 60s and add minimum closed duration to prevent flip-flopping. 3) Load-shedding: add region-level proportional shedding (slo/enforcer/load_shed_policy.go) that steps down traffic based on per-route error budget burn rate. 4) Circuit breaker ordering: prefer local shedding -> model fallbacks -> regional failover (configurable). 5) Observability: emit slo.enforcer.backoff.state, slo.enforcer.load_shed.pct and slo.enforcer.failover.trigger_reason for faster debugging. 6) Tests: add deterministic unit tests and a new integration canary for regional failover choreography. Rollout: hotfix merged to main and auto-cherry-picked to release/2026-02. Risk: medium - changes touch the enforcer state machine but include conservative defaults and feature-flag gating. Rollback: revert to previous commit and remove feature flag to restore original behavior. Related: follows up on ENG-8123 and the incident runbook improvements in PR #472900.
